title: Albin Countergambit: the ideas
line: Black offers a pawn of its own and wedges a pawn deep into White's camp.

steps.text: White starts by pushing the pawn in front of its queen two squares, into the center.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares too. It holds the center.

also.g8f6: That is the start of the Indian defenses, also sound. This lesson pushes the pawn.

steps.after: White offers a side pawn to pull your center pawn away. This is the Queen's Gambit.

steps.text: Push the pawn in front of your king two squares. You offer a pawn of your own.

also.e7e6: That is the Queen's Gambit Declined, a calmer choice. This lesson plays the gambit.
also.c7c6: That is the Slav Defense, a calmer choice. This lesson plays the gambit.
also.d5c4: That is the Queen's Gambit Accepted, also sound. This lesson plays the gambit.

steps.after: This is the Albin Countergambit. It gives up a little for surprise and open play. White takes the pawn.

steps.text: Push your center pawn one square. It wedges into White's camp and keeps the knight off c3.
Bring the knight out. It guards the pawn on d4 and attacks the pawn on e5.
Bring the other knight out. It heads for g6, to attack the pawn on e5 a second time.
Move the knight on to g6. Now two knights attack the pawn on e5.
steps.after: White castles. Two knights attack the pawn on e5, and only the knight on f3 guards it.

steps.text: Take the pawn on e5 with the knight from g6.

also.f8e7: Developing first is sound too. This lesson takes the pawn back now.

steps.text: Take back with the other knight, so the material is level.
steps.after: The gambit pawn is back. Your pawn on d4 still cramps White, and the knight sits in the center.

summary: Black gives a pawn for a cramping pawn in the center, then brings both knights to take it back.
